title: Deploying to Mobile & Edge 📱
description: Integrate a TFLite model into an Android/iOS app and run inference on‑device.

slides.title: From .tflite to an App 📲
slides.content:
# The Mobile Integration Path

1. **Train** a TF model and export to SavedModel.
2. **Convert** to .tflite with desired optimizations.
3. **Add** the .tflite file to your mobile project (Android: `assets/`; iOS: bundle).
4. **Use** the TFLite Interpreter API to run inference.

TensorFlow provides native SDKs for Android (Java/Kotlin) and iOS (Swift/Objective‑C).

slides.title: Android (Kotlin) Inference Snippet
slides.content: Conceptual code of how you'd load and run a TFLite model.

quizData.question: What is the role of the TFLite Interpreter on mobile?

options.text: To train the model on the device
To execute the converted model and run inference

quizData.explanation: The Interpreter is a lightweight runtime that loads and executes .tflite models.

slides.title: On‑Device Benefits 🏠
slides.content:
# Why Run Locally?
- **Latency**: no network round‑trip; real‑time.
- **Privacy**: data stays on device.
- **Offline**: works without internet.
- **Cost**: no server costs.

Ideal for image classification, speech recognition, object detection in camera apps, etc.

slides.title: iOS (Swift) Snippet
Use GPU Delegates 🚄
slides.content: Both Android and iOS support GPU acceleration for TFLite. Add a GPU delegate to the interpreter to speed up compute‑intensive models significantly.

slides.title: Try It 🛠️
slides.content: Convert a small MNIST model to TFLite, write a Python script that loads and runs it using the TFLite interpreter (`tf.lite.Interpreter`) to verify correctness. (No mobile device required).
